_meta.description: Small hand-written query/ground-truth set for himanshmunjal/Ephemeral-share, built specifically to measure retrieval quality across a POLYGLOT repo (Go backend + JS frontend) after Go ingestion support was added. Unlike eval_dataset.json (single-language repos), every query here has its true answer in exactly one language, so Precision@5 directly measures whether the retriever/reranker favors one language over the other for reasons unrelated to relevance.
_meta.grounding_note: File paths and function names were fetched live via `gh api repos/himanshmunjal/Ephemeral-share/contents/...` against the default branch at dataset-authoring time (2026-09-08). Re-verify before reuse if the upstream repo has since changed.
_meta.purpose: Baseline this dataset against the CURRENT embedder (microsoft/codebert-base) + reranker (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) to get a real Precision@5 number, then re-run after any candidate model swap + full re-index to measure actual uplift instead of one-off similarity spot checks.

queries.query: Where is the shared session data stored temporarily and how does it expire?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: Store.CreateSession in backend/internal/redisclient/store.go marshals the session into a sessionRecord and writes it to Redis with an absolute TTL (s.ttl) via a TxPipeline Set/Expire, so the record is automatically purged by Redis once the session's time limit is reached.

queries.query: What background process removes expired sessions and their files?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: CleanupWorker.PeriodicSweep in backend/internal/handlers/cleanup.go runs on an interval, calling cleanupSession for expired sessions to purge Redis keys and delete associated S3 objects and analytics state.

queries.query: How does the backend prevent a single client from sending too many requests?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: RateLimit in backend/internal/middleware/ratelimit.go returns a gin.HandlerFunc that tracks a per-client rate.Limiter (keyed by visitor) and rejects requests once the configured per-minute quota is exceeded.

queries.query: How are live WebSocket connections for a session managed and broadcast to?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: Hub.broadcast in backend/internal/ws/hub.go sends a payload to every registered connection for a session's hub, with Register/Unregister managing which connections are currently subscribed.

queries.query: Where is the end-to-end encryption key generated on the client?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: generateSessionKey in frontend/src/lib/crypto.js uses the Web Crypto API (crypto.subtle.generateKey) to create a new AES key entirely in the browser, so the key never touches the server unencrypted.

queries.query: How is the shareable session link constructed with the encryption key embedded?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: shareLink in frontend/src/pages/SessionRoomPage.jsx builds the session URL and appends the base64 encryption key as a `#k=...` URL fragment, which browsers never send to the server.

queries.query: What happens on the client when a user submits the create-session form?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: handleCreate in frontend/src/pages/CreateSessionPage.jsx generates the session key, calls the create-session API, stores the key locally via storeKey, and marks the current user as the session owner.

queries.query: What calls Store.CreateSession, and what would break if its signature changed?
queries.ground_truth_answer_summary: SessionHandler.CreateSession in backend/internal/handlers/session.go is the HTTP handler that calls Store.CreateSession after validating and constructing the session model — changing Store.CreateSession's signature breaks this call site directly.
